info.title: API: Mapping
info.description: Hotel and room mapping APIs. Map partner hotel IDs to LiteAPI catalogue hotels, and map or group supplier room names against your room catalog. Room matching: **Implementation Workflow** (`implementation-workflow`).

partner.description: Partner name. Pass this exact string as the `partner` form field when mapping IDs (matching is case-insensitive upstream).

mappings.description: Number of known ID mappings for this partner — a proxy for inventory coverage size.

MappingSummary.description: Outcome counts returned in the `X-Mapping-Summary` response header after a partner ID mapping run.

matched.description: Rows successfully mapped to Nuitee inventory

review.description: Rows that need manual review (ambiguous candidates)

not_found.description: Partner IDs with no match in Nuitee inventory

invalid.description: Rows that could not be parsed or validated

input_gcs.description: GCS URI of the input CSV

output_gcs.description: Optional GCS URI for the result CSV

i.description: Supplier row index (stable within the request)

predictedLabel.description: 1 if the candidate is a positive match at the decision threshold, otherwise 0

selected.description: Best match when status is mapped; null otherwise

name.description: Mapped reference room name, or not_mapped when rejected

id.description: Mapped reference room id, or 0 when not mapped

reason.description: Short human explanation when not mapped
reason.example: Run-of-house rate; no specific room type

previous.description: Prior cache mapping for this room, if any

reason.description: Short human explanation when not mapped

source.description: How the final decision was produced

modelOutput.description: Candidate scores retained for transparency; null for exact-match and run-of-house rooms

type.description: Normalised bed type. Labels are canonicalised: 'Extra-large double bed (Super-king size)' becomes extra_large_double, 'Queen bed' becomes queen.

label.description: Bed description as stated by the source.

count.description: Number of beds of this type.

RoomAttributes.description: Optional structured evidence about a room. Omitted fields mean the source did not state them, never that the room lacks them. Normalised on submit: enum values are lower-cased and trimmed, m2/m² are folded into sqm, and string lists are deduplicated. Unknown structure, bedRelation or size.unit values, negative counts and non-positive sizes return 400. At most 4 KiB per room's attributes and 256 KiB across a list.

structure.description: Room structure as stated by the source. Do not infer it from a marketing room name.

tier.description: Commercial tier stated by the source (standard, premium, deluxe, ...).

bedrooms.description: Stated bedroom count for multi-room structures. 0 or omitted means not stated.

bedRelation.description: Whether the listed beds are all present (and), alternatives (or), or a single configuration (none).

size.description: Stated floor area, normalised to square metres.

unit.description: Square metres. m2 and m² are folded into sqm on submit.

views.description: Normalised view labels. 'City View' and 'city' converge on city.

accessibility.description: Normalised accessibility features stated by the source (for example mobility_accessible, roll_in_shower). Never inferred from a room name.

features.description: Only attributes the source stated as true or false; a missing key means unknown, not false. Informational, never gates a match.

amenities.description: Optional amenity list for audit context. Informational; never gates a match.

get.summary: List partners available for hotel ID mapping
get.description:
## Overview

Returns every partner that can be used for hotel ID mapping, along with each partner's inventory coverage size (`mappings`). Use this list to discover which partner inventories can be aligned with Nuitee / liteAPI hotel IDs.

Hotel mapping connects a partner's hotel identifiers to Nuitee catalogue IDs so you can shop, book, and enrich content against a single inventory.

## When to Use

- **Before mapping IDs** - Confirm the partner name to pass into `POST /hotels/match/partners/with-id`
- **Coverage checks** - Compare `mappings` counts to estimate how much of a partner's inventory is already linked
- **Partner selectors** - Populate UI or automation dropdowns with supported partners
- **Onboarding** - Discover which OTAs / suppliers are available for ID-to-ID mapping

## What You Get

- **Partner names** - Exact strings to send as the `partner` form field on the map endpoint
- **Inventory size** - `mappings` count per partner (known ID links in the mapping catalogue)
- **Sorted list** - Partners ordered by mapping count, descending

## Key Features

- **No request body**: Simple authenticated GET
- **Case-insensitive partner names upstream**: Prefer the exact `partner` string from this response
- **Accounts without suppliers**: Allowed to call hotel mapping endpoints (standard auth still applies)

## Quick Start

1. Authenticate with your LiteAPI `X-API-Key`
2. Call `GET /hotels/match/partners`
3. Pick a `partner` value from the response
4. Upload that partner's hotel ID CSV to `POST /hotels/match/partners/with-id`

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

200.description: Partner list with inventory mapping counts

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid API key

post.summary: Map partner hotel IDs to Nuitee inventory
post.description:
## Overview

Maps a specific partner's hotel inventory to Nuitee / liteAPI catalogue IDs. Upload a CSV of partner hotel IDs and receive a result CSV that links each row to Nuitee property identifiers.

This is the synchronous **partner ID → Nuitee ID** mapping path. Processing runs in one request: CSV in, mapped CSV out (plus an `X-Mapping-Summary` header with outcome counts).

## When to Use

- **Partner inventory alignment** - Convert Booking.com, Expedia, or other partner hotel IDs into Nuitee `core_property_id` / `lite_property_id`
- **Bulk ID resolution** - Map large partner ID lists in a single call
- **Coverage analysis** - Use `matched`, `review`, `not_found`, and `invalid` counts from `X-Mapping-Summary`
- **Content & rates pipelines** - Resolve partner IDs before search, booking, or enrichment against Nuitee inventory

## What You Get

- **Result CSV** - Per-row mapping outcomes with columns such as `input_id`, `status`, `resolution`, `core_property_id`, `lite_property_id`, `candidate_core_ids`
- **Summary header** - `X-Mapping-Summary` JSON with `rows`, `matched`, `review`, `not_found`, `invalid`
- **Download filename** - `Content-Disposition` attachment name from the server (for example `id-mapping-Expedia.csv`)

## Key Features

- **Partner-scoped**: Mapping runs against one partner inventory at a time (`partner` form field)
- **Flexible CSV input**: Single ID column (with or without header), or multi-column files with a recognized ID header
- **Optional geo columns**: Latitude/longitude improve resolution when partner IDs are ambiguous
- **Streamed response**: Result CSV is streamed; there is no `{"data": ...}` JSON wrapper

## Quick Start

1. Call `GET /hotels/match/partners` and copy the partner name
2. Prepare a CSV of that partner's hotel IDs
3. `POST` `multipart/form-data` with:
   - `partner` — partner name from step 1
   - `file` — the CSV
4. Save the response body as CSV and read `X-Mapping-Summary` for counts

**Accepted ID column names** (case-insensitive): `id`, `hotel_id`, `hotelid`, `hotel_code`, `provider_id`, `provider_hotel_id`, `provider_property_id`, `partner_id`, `partner_hotel_id`, `property_id`, `code`.

**Example curl:**

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url "https://api.liteapi.travel/v3.0/hotels/match/partners/with-id" \
  --header "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  --form "partner=Booking.com" \
  --form "file=@/path/to/partner-ids.csv;type=text/csv"
```

Authenticate with your LiteAPI `X-API-Key`.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

**Platform note:** Cloud Run and the global load balancer cap request/response bodies at 32 MiB. Larger uploads may not fully pass through this API hop.

partner.description: Partner name from GET /hotels/match/partners. Selects which partner inventory to map against Nuitee.

file.description: CSV of partner hotel IDs to map to Nuitee inventory

200.description: Result CSV mapping partner IDs to Nuitee inventory

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the result CSV

400.description: Bad Request — missing partner, unknown partner, or unreadable CSV

value.error: could not find an id column; …

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid API key

post.summary: Submit an async hotel-match batch job
post.description:
## Overview

Upload an onboarding CSV of hotel rows (name, country, optional address/coordinates) and start an async **content-based** hotel matching job. Returns immediately with a `job_id` to poll.

Use this when partner hotel IDs are unavailable and you need to match hotels by content against Nuitee inventory.

## When to Use

- **Bulk onboarding** - Match many hotels by name/location when partner IDs are not available
- **Large files** - Jobs above the inline row limit are processed via chunked workers
- **GCS workflows** - Submit with `input_gcs` / `output_gcs` for large files outside the API body limit

## What You Get

- **202 Accepted** - Initial `JobStatus` with `status: queued` and `job_id`
- **Progress polling** - Use `GET /hotels/match/async/jobs/{jobId}/status` until `status` is `done` or `error`
- **Result CSV** - Download via `GET /hotels/match/async/jobs/{jobId}` when complete

## Quick Start

1. POST `multipart/form-data` with `file` (CSV), or JSON `{ "input_gcs": "gs://..." }` for large files
2. Poll status with the returned `job_id`
3. Download the result CSV when `status` is `done`

Input CSV must include `name` and `country` columns (accepted header aliases vary upstream). Optional `output_gcs` writes the result directly to GCS instead of returning CSV through the API.

Authenticate with your LiteAPI `X-API-Key`.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

**Platform note:** Multipart uploads are capped at 32 MiB through this API hop — use GCS input mode for larger files.

output_gcs.description: Optional GCS URI for the result CSV

example.error: CSV exceeds 32MiB; use input_gcs for large files

get.description:
## Overview

Returns the current progress and verdict counts for an async hotel-match job.

## When to Use

- **Poll after submit** - Call repeatedly until `status` is `done` or `error`

## What You Get

- **Job counters** - `total`, `done`, `matched`, `review`, `no_match`, and conflict-class counts
- **Terminal states** - `done` means the result is ready (unless `output_gcs` was set); `error` includes an `error` message

## Quick Start

Use the `job_id` from the submit response.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

## Overview

Streams the finished result CSV for a completed async hotel-match job.

## When to Use

- **After job completes** - Call when status polling returns `status: done` and no `output_gcs` was requested at submit time

## What You Get

- **Result CSV** - One row per input hotel with verdict, matched IDs, scores, and reasons
- **Attachment header** - `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="hotel-match-{jobId}.csv"`

## Quick Start

Poll until `status` is `done`, then download this endpoint. If submit included `output_gcs`, read that URI instead — this endpoint returns **409**.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the result CSV

404.description: Unknown job or result not ready

value.error: result not available (job still running or expired)

post.summary: Match supplier rooms to a reference catalog
post.description:
**What it does:** For each supplier room, returns the best **reference room** match with confidence scores and ranked alternatives.

**Workflow role:** Optional **step 0** — quick sync scoring before async hotel jobs.

**Use when:** You need an **immediate** answer with `suppliers`. Either send `references` yourself, **or** omit `references` and set **`hotelId`** so the service resolves the catalog (`room_mapping_catalog` → LiteAPI data API; your references win if supplied; max 500 rooms).

**Do not use when:** You need persisted mappings, audit reasons, or room attributes — use `POST /rooms/match/async`. Not for clustering without a catalog — use `POST /rooms/group`.

**If `references` is omitted:** missing `hotelId` or unresolvable catalog → **400**; Redis or data API failure → **500**; suppliers×references over upstream cap → **413** when configured.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

hotelId.description: Hotel ID used to resolve the reference catalog when `references` is omitted. Required in that case; echoed in the response.

threshold.description: Minimum confidence score for a positive match

topK.description: Number of ranked candidates returned per supplier

references.description: Optional. Allowed mapping targets (the catalog). Omit or send empty to resolve the hotel catalog from `room_mapping_catalog:{hotelId}` (dispatcher-owned, read-only here), then the LiteAPI data API. Caller-supplied rooms win. Resolved catalogs are capped upstream (default 500) and never truncated; `hotelId` is required when this is omitted.

post.summary: Submit an async room mapping job
post.description:
**What it does:** Starts a **background mapping job** for one hotel (`jobId` to poll).

**Workflow role:** **Step 1** — create or refresh hotel mappings.

**Use when:** Hotel onboarding, catalog refresh, or sending trusted **attributes** (`supplierRooms`, optional `referenceRooms`, `attributeDetail`).

**Do not use when:** You only need instant sync scores — use `POST /rooms/match`.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

referenceRooms.description: Optional. Allowed mapping targets (the catalog). Omit or send empty to score against our hotel catalog, which the service resolves automatically. When supplied, the caller's list wins. Rejected above 500 rooms; the same limit applies to the catalog resolved on your behalf. Attributes are optional per room.

roomNames.description: Supplier room names to map. Blank entries are dropped and normalized duplicates are removed. Max 100 after deduplication. Ignored when `supplierRooms` is non-empty.

supplierRooms.description: Attribute-bearing supplier rooms. When non-empty it replaces `roomNames`. Blank names are dropped and normalized duplicates removed; max 100 after deduplication. Sending attributes lets the audit treat our own catalog attributes as evidence on both sides.

attributeDetail.description: How much attribute context the audit receives. `none` sends names only; `summary` (default) sends structure, tier, bedrooms, beds, bedRelation, occupancy, size, views and accessibility; `full` adds features, amenities and source. Applies to both supplier and reference attributes. The full request is always stored on the job.

400.description: Bad Request - malformed JSON or validation failure. Also returned when `hotelId` is missing, when neither `roomNames` nor a non-empty `supplierRooms` is supplied, when `referenceRooms` is omitted and no catalog can be resolved for the hotel, when a room attribute is invalid (unknown `structure`, `bedRelation` or `size.unit`, negative counts, non-positive sizes, an empty `beds[].type`), when attributes exceed 4 KiB per room or 256 KiB per list, when `attributeDetail` is unknown, or when the supplied or automatically resolved catalog exceeds 500 rooms.

value.error: deep-map validation error: hotelId is required
deep-map validation error: referenceRooms was not provided and the hotel catalog could not be resolved; provide referenceRooms or retry later
deep-map validation error: supplierRooms[0].attributes: structure "loft" is not one of: room, suite, studio, apartment, villa, penthouse
deep-map validation error: fetched catalog exceeds max of 500

409.description: Conflict - a deep-map job is already in flight for this hotel

example.error: deep-map job already in flight for hotel: dm_1777386480123456789_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8

500.description: Internal Server Error. Also returned as `failed to resolve reference rooms` when `referenceRooms` was omitted and the hotel data API could not be reached.

get.summary: Get async room mapping job status
get.description:
**What it does:** Job **status** and per-room **`confirm` / `remap` / reject** with `reasonCode`.

**Workflow role:** **Step 2** — poll every 5–10 s after async submit.

**Use when:** You have a `jobId`.

**Do not use when:** You only need the saved dictionary — use `GET /rooms/match/async/matches/{hotelId}`.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

currentMappingCount.description: Number of mappings available before this job ran.

supplierRooms.description: Supplier rooms as stored on the job, including attributes when they were supplied.

attributeDetail.description: Detail level used for the audit. Defaults to summary.

get.summary: Get saved room mappings for a hotel
get.description:
**What it does:** **Saved mapping dictionary** for your account and hotel.

**Workflow role:** **Step 3** — runtime lookup after mappings exist.

**Use when:** Resolving supplier names in search or book.

**Do not use when:** You need audit detail — use the job endpoint.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

post.summary: Group rooms without a reference catalog
post.description:
**What it does:** Clusters supplier room names **without** a reference catalog.

**Workflow role:** Outside the main four-step flow — exploration only.

**Use when:** You do not have catalog rooms yet.

**Do not use when:** You have a catalog — use `/rooms/match` or async.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

debug.description: When true, returns parsed entities per room

propertyId.description: Stable property identifier in your catalog

createGroups.description: Must be true to enable clustering

outputAggregation.description: Attributes used to form groups. Recommended: roomClass, roomType, bedType, roomView

supplierRooms.description: Rooms from that supplier for this property

roomName.description: Raw room title from the supplier feed

post.description:
**What it does:** Assigns each supplier room to **one reference bucket**.

**Workflow role:** Alternate **sync** view (not step 0 of the main flow).

**Use when:** You want reference-centric grouping instead of per-supplier scores.

**Do not use when:** You need ranked candidates or async persistence.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

hotelId.description: Correlation ID echoed in the response

threshold.description: Minimum score to attach a supplier to a reference group
